tools.name: probe

question.description: The single quiz question to ask. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next question.

label.description: Display label for the answer option — a bare claim, no reasoning

value.description: Optional machine-readable value returned for the option. Defaults to the label.

options.description: REQUIRED. The answer options (2 or more) as a JSON ARRAY of option objects — never a JSON-encoded string. Options only — there is no free-text mode. Give each option a stable `value`; you reference the correct one by that value in correctAnswer. Never add your own 'I don't know' option — that choice is added for you.

multiSelect.description: Set to true when more than one option is correct and the learner must select all of them.

explanation.description: REQUIRED. Explanation revealed AFTER the learner answers (shown whether they got it right or wrong). Use it to reinforce why the correct answer is correct. It is written BEFORE correctAnswer by design: reason it out first, then commit the answer the reasoning supports.

correctAnswer.description: REQUIRED. The correct answer as the option value(s) — the `value` field of the option you intend. Single-select: a single string (e.g. "mercury"). Multi-select: an array of strings (e.g. ["belize", "niue"]); the learner is only correct if their selection matches this set exactly. Always pass the value, not a position number — this is self-checking and prevents miscounting. A value that matches no option fails validation and the call is returned to you to fix.

details.description: Optional extra context or instructions shown under the question.

tools.name: quiz

type.description: REQUIRED — the question's role in the teaching cycle, as a bare word (no quotes): predict = posed BEFORE you teach the step (its own turn; the learner answers, then your teaching resolves it — arrives open, never collapsed); check = posed AFTER the step's teaching is complete (arrives collapsed behind the Check your understanding reveal). ONE question per turn either way.

nodeId.description: REQUIRED plan-tree node id this question is about — must EXACTLY match one of this session's plan_init node slugs (validated at call time; a mismatched id is rejected back to you). The lesson's position on the map derives from these tags (the node the latest tagged question is about is where the map stands; earlier ones count as visited). A node takes as many questions as it deserves: stay on one node for as many turns as the understanding needs — one reasoning step at a time, never rush forward. For off-map checks use ask_user_question.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the learner a single question and pause until they answer. NOT graded — there is no correct answer. Use when requirements are ambiguous, preferences are needed, a decision would materially affect the lesson, or you need an open-ended response. ONE question per turn: call a single ask_user_question, then end your turn — his answer determines the next.

question.description: The single question to ask the learner. ONE question per turn: ask, then end your turn — the answer determines the next question.

details.description: Optional extra context or instructions shown under the question.

label.description: Display label for the answer option — a bare claim, no reasoning

value.description: Optional machine-readable value returned for the option. Defaults to the label.

description.description: Optional extra detail shown below the option

options.description: Optional multiple-choice options. Omit for free-form text input. The learner can always choose 'Other' and type a custom answer when options are provided.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow multiple answers to the same question.

tools.name: probe_done
tools.description: Conclude the probing phase and hand off to the teaching phase. Call this ONCE, when the probe is complete: every strand the lesson depends on is bracketed (a floor he reliably gets right AND a ceiling where it runs out), and his learning goal is concrete. The input IS the learner assessment — one strand per dependency the lesson will rest on, with your read of where his edge sits on it (floor, ceiling, misconceptions, what to build from). It streams to the learner live and becomes the handoff artifact the teacher plans from. Refused while a question is still open, and after the probe is already concluded. After it succeeds, say your closing sentence and end your turn.

strand.description: The dependency strand (e.g. 'the derivative as a limit') — a name the plan can hang a node on.

assessment.description: Where his edge sits on this strand: the floor (what he reliably gets right), the ceiling (where it runs out), misconceptions found, and what the lesson should build from.

strands.description: Every strand the planned lesson will depend on, each with your read of his edge on it.

summary.description: Optional overall synthesis: his apparent goal and where the teaching should enter.

assessment.description: The learner assessment — the probe's distilled output.

tools.name: plan_init
tools.description: Write or REWRITE this session's plan map — the dependency graph the learner follows live in the plan window. Call once right after the probe concludes, to present the map; re-call whenever the map is wrong (the new block replaces the old tree). A mermaid graph block (any direction): one node per line (`slug[Short Title]` — slugs are permanent lowercase ids: a-z, 0-9, hyphens/underscores), `-->` edges meaning 'from must be understood before to' (chains fine). 5–15 nodes: a map, not a syllabus — one reasoning step per node, compress. Every check you fire names the node it assesses via `nodeId`; where the lesson stands derives from those tags.

mermaid.description:
A mermaid graph block (any direction), e.g.:
graph TD
  primitives[Number primitives] --> operators[Arithmetic operators] --> expressions[Evaluating expressions]
The only strict rule: ids are permanent lowercase slugs (a-z, 0-9, hyphens/underscores) — checks reference them via nodeId. Titles are free single-line text; `-->` means 'from = prerequisite' (chains fine); no subgraphs, styles, or classes.

tools.name: problem
tools.description: Pose one practice problem. Ends the turn — the learner works in the thinking field; their thinking traces and answer commits arrive back as labeled messages. The modelSolution rides this call's arguments and stays hidden from the learner until you conclude (conclude shows it verbatim — the reveal needs no new field). Only one problem may be active — conclude it before posing the next.

statement.description: REQUIRED — the problem as the learner sees it (markdown + LaTeX). Must be self-contained and solvable from the session's material. NEVER announces the target proposition.

mode.description: REQUIRED — the demand mode: recall, discrimination, or composition (bare words, no quotes).

target.description: The proposition id(s) this problem exercises, from the session context's [id] list — include when the material is in the map; OMIT entirely when it is not (a topic session poses untagged problems). Names are normalized to ids at the seam; an unknown proposition is rejected.

modelSolution.description: REQUIRED — the full solution, moves in order, committed BEFORE the learner sees the problem. This IS the reveal — conclude shows it verbatim; never re-author it.

tools.name: conclude
tools.description: Conclude the active problem: records the outcome + verdict, reveals the committed solution, and frees the learner's composer. After the result, say your closing words about the learner's work if useful, then END YOUR TURN — no further tool calls. The next problem is NEVER posed here: it waits for the learner's explicit go-ahead (a *Next problem* message, or their own words asking for the next one). Between problems, answer their questions about the concluded one. Nothing may conclude unless a problem is active.

outcome.description: REQUIRED — the outcome: solved, solvedWithHints, movedOn, or surrendered — bare words, no quotes (dismissed is synthesized, never yours).

verdict.description: REQUIRED — the plain-language verdict: what was credited, where it broke. On a wrong answer: localize the break, do NOT give the correction.

rung.description: REQUIRED — the hint-ladder rung the problem needed: R0 through R5, or null = no hint was given (bare, no quotes).

missClass.description: REQUIRED — the miss classification: cue, discrimination, execution, careless, or structural — or null = no miss (bare, no quotes).

retest.description: REQUIRED — true marks the problem for a fresh-surface retest before the session ends.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List the sessions of the learner's persistent knowledge graph — every chat or imported-notes file that ever contributed a proposition, most recent first. The map is organized into birth-session clusters (propositions grouped by the session they were first learned in), and session names are those clusters' labels. Each line: the session's name, kind (chat/file), how many propositions were born in it, its dates, and its id — use that id with list_propositions. Reading this first shows what he has already covered and when, before you probe anything.

tools.name: list_propositions
tools.description: List the propositions BORN in one knowledge-graph session — what was covered there. Names only — no statement text, no session contents (owner ruling 2026-09-23: the map's ORGANIZATION is your business, its prose is not).

session.description: The session's id exactly as list_sessions reported it (a chat id or a notes source id)

tools.name: vault_search
tools.description: Search the learner's Obsidian vault (markdown notes in iCloud) by words. Returns up to 10 matching notes with their vault-relative paths and a few matching lines each. Use it to recall what the learner has written or saved before; follow up with vault_read for the full note.

query.description: Words to look for (case-insensitive). Notes matching more of the words rank higher.

tools.name: vault_read
tools.description: Read one note from the learner's Obsidian vault by its vault-relative path (as vault_search reported it). Long notes are truncated.

tools.name: vault_write
tools.description: Write a markdown note into the app's own folder of the learner's Obsidian vault (Notestrand/). Notes elsewhere in the vault can never be modified. Use it when the learner asks you to remember something (append to Memory.md), or to save notes they ask for. Obsidian [[wikilinks]] work.

path.description: Path relative to the Notestrand/ folder, ending in .md, e.g. "Memory.md" or "Notes/Fourier.md".

append.description: true appends to the end of the note (created if missing); false or omitted replaces the note.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current or specific information: facts that may have changed (prices, rules, dates, statistics, news, latest versions) or that you are not sure of. Returns titles, URLs and snippets. Check the learner's vault first when the question is about their own notes or course; use this for everything else that needs to be accurate. Open the most relevant results with web_fetch before relying on them, and name your sources.

query.description: A focused search query, like you would type into a search engine.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Open a public web page (http or https) and return its readable text, truncated if long. Use it for a URL the learner gives you or one found with web_search. Never put the learner's private notes or personal details into a URL.

url.description: The full URL, starting with https:// or http://.
